Duration::total().seconds()¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

DurationTotal Duration::total() const;
Series DurationTotal::seconds() const;

What It Does¶

Converts a Duration’s elapsed magnitude into a plain Series expressed in seconds — total().nanoseconds() divided by 1e9. This is the way out of duration-space back into an ordinary numeric Series, e.g. for storing elapsed time in a DataFrame column (recall Duration itself isn’t a ThreadKind payload — see the API reference overview) or feeding it into arithmetic that doesn’t care about the duration/instant distinction. See total().nanoseconds() for the full explanation of the total() accessor.

Parameters¶

None — this is a zero-argument accessor on self.

Returns¶

Series A floating-point Series at self’s shape, in seconds.

Examples¶

Example 1. A 90-minute Duration read as seconds.

auto ninety_min = pluss::duration::minutes(90);
std::cout << pluss::series::print(ninety_min.total().seconds());

Output¶

Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=5400.0000

90 minutes is 5400 seconds.

Notes¶

  • .total().seconds() never rounds or truncates — the result is always the exact (floating-point) division.

  • To go the other direction (a number of seconds back into a Duration), use pluss::duration::seconds.

See Also¶

  • total().milliseconds(): the finer unit this divides.

  • total().minutes(): the next unit up.

  • construction: the inverse direction.
